VIKKI CARR is hailed as one of the top, new international cabaret
artists. She has appeared at London's ‘Talk Of The Town’, ‘The
Cocoanut Grove' in Los Angeles, 'The Sands’ in Las Vegas and ‘The
Persian Room’ in New York. She has made regular appearances on all
the major television shows in America, recorded three “VIKKI CARR
SHOWS” for BBC Television in Britain and has had to refuse offers
for a starring role in a Broadway musical due to her solidly booked
schedule.

Born of Mexican-American parents in El Paso, Texas VIKKI grew
up speaking Spanish before she could speak English and singing in
both languages for her family. At school and college she sang in the
choirs and with instrumental combos for evening dances. After grad-
uation VIKKI joined a Mexican-Irish band and sang her way through
Reno, Las Vegas, Lake Tahoe and Hawaii before recording a demon-
stration disc which she took to LIBERTY RECORDS. Her first single {
secured modest success in the U.S.A. and became a huge hit in
Australia which resulted in her first foreign tour. Since then her sub-
sequent singles and albums have registered strong sales both at home
and abroad.

The petite, vivacious VIKKI CARR is now in frequent demand not
only in America but throughout much of the world. Home is in Beverly
Hills, California, with her law student husband and “a rather spoilt
Yorkshire terrier", but says VIKKI “I don't seem to be there for very
long, because my work schedule is so full, but | am not complaining, |
am getting the best of both worlds at the moment and on both sides
of the Atlantic too!

This latest album from VIKKH CARR takes its title from.the song
that marked her début in the British ChartsIT MUST BE HIM. The
eleven other songs included, will introduce the new enthusiast to some
of the many different aspects of this talented vocalist, and establish
her even further in the hearts of her confirmed followers, for the magic
of VIKKI CARR is really SOMETHING!

‘Steeds als ik André Hazes hoor zingen, gaan de wolken voor de zon vandaan. Now
weet ik wel: dit is een zin die nogal hoogdravend aandoet, maar ook zit er een
kern van waarheid in. André doet mij altijd even mijn zorgen vergeten, want het
komt uit zijn hart wat hij doet en af en toe zelfs uit zijn tenen maar nooit uit
zijn duim want daarvoor zijn zijn teksten te echt en te reéel.
Ook deze nieuwe L.P. van André zal zijn weg naar de vele fans zeker weten .
te vinden, daar hoef ik niet toe aan te sporen. Zal ik al die fans eens vragen. —~
om niet altijd deze liedjes heerlijk mee te lallen, maar ook eens goed naar
gle teksten te luisteren, want het zijn stuk voor stuk briljantjes.
Kogisch want met veel zorg en liefde heeft André samen met Tim Griek
* (producer) aan deze plaat gewerkt.
‘Dat zal U een zorg zijn ‘hien, maar het is ook belangrijk want je
~~ kunt het horen en dat een plaat nu eenmaal het belangrijkste,
dat je het kunt horen.

André van Duin.

In the world of music today, an outstanding instrumentalist is not necessarily an
exciting entertainer at the same time. A new young pianist, who has been described
as a flawless and imaginative artist, has bridged the gap between techhical perfection
and entertainment magic with relative ease, resulting in a full and complete personality
with charm and style as well as technique .. . his name is PETER NERO.

This tall, slim, sensitively handsome man, who has emerged as an artist of con-
summate skill, was born in New York City, started at the keyboard at the age of seven
and by the time he was fourteen he was the recipient of numerous awards, had made
symphony hall appearances and was the possessor of a Juilliard Scholarship. He went
on to Brooklyn College, where he graduated to invade the music world as a winner
of TV talent contests and as a promising concert pianist. ;

Peter Nero has a unique blending of classical music and jazz in all his arrange-
ments. He has developed a love for jazz and pop music and has adapted all of these
facets of his musical knowledge to his piano playing. You never hear the constant
sameness in any rendition he plays, therefore, he is constantly creating something new.

In the nation’s leading concert theatres and in the recording world, the name of
Peter Nero has become synonymous with an exciting style and unique form of musical
expression that holds the attention of not only musical aficionados, but the average
layman as well.

The ever-growing corps of Nero disciples attests amply to the fact that here
indeed is a musical artist to be reckoned with, a man of imagination and verve, who
is always striving to become a finer, more versatile and, most important, a thinking
and dynamically aware performing artist , . . here then is the terrific Peter Nero.

Also starring on this album is the well known artist Mike De Napoli, one of the
finest pianists to ever hit the ivories,

important variety shows and selective television specials, He has scored and arranged
the music for several films, his blueprint now includes composing for the Broadway
musical theatre,

of his single “IT’S NOT UNUSUAL” created a great demand
for his unique singing talent. He achieved international success
@s an artist when he crossed the Atlantic to appear on all the
major American T.V. network shows. He also toured the
Country for over three months appearing on one-night stands.
During this exciting but exhausting tour he met the king of
rock-and-roll, Elvis Presley, in Los Angeles.
Whilst on this tour his next record "WHAT'S NEW PUSSY-
CAT?” was released and quickly climbed and occupied a high
position in the charts. His first LP “ALONG CAME JONES”
re-titied for the U.S. market “IT’S NOT UNUSUAL” had been
such a tremendous success that another LP was rush-released
entitled “WHAT'S NEW PUSSYCAT?” (not released in Bri-
tain). This also was snapped up quickly by the avid fans.
Apart from the success of his records Tom is first to admit
that the experience he gained during his three months touring
in America was invaluable. Being unable to take his backing
group The Squires with him was a bad blow for Tom. They
have been with him from the start of his career and during
this time a sympathetic rapport between singer and musicians
has developed. This intuitive unterstanding of each other's
abilities has led to a successful partnership enabling Tom to
devote all his attention to the delivery and performance of the
songs.
Being bereft of The Squires Tom had to rely on various backing
groups as he went from one venue to another, These engage-
ments were often hundreds of miles apart and most of Tom's
waking hours were devoured by the extensive travelling, leay-
ing hardly any time for rehearsals with the latest backing
roup before the curtain went up.
t is an indication of the talent that Tom possesses that the
many hours of travelling, snatched meals and inadequate
rehearsal time had no effect on the quality of his performance
on stage. His performances on records, television shows and
personal appearances impressed everyone during his stay,

world without suffering the encumbrance of oxygen tanks etc.
Eventually even the most enthusiastic snorkeler has to return
to shore and gradually the LP was set up.

On his return to Britain in November he entered the recording
studio for two weeks’ strenuous work starting at 10 a.m. until
late at night. Nevertheless the result is a very interesting LP.
The choice of material this time is mostly original songs plus
some specially written for him by his manager Gordon Mills
and arranger Les Reed.

THE STUDENT PRINCE

Mario

‘Somebody once wrote—come to think of it, it was this writer—
that songwriters have the most colorful obituaries. The reason
is obvious. Memories never die.

‘When the Shuberts first debuted Sigmund Romberg’s The Stu-
dent Prince (In Heidelberg)—to give it its full, original title—
opening on December 2, 1924 at the old Jolson’s 59th Street
‘Theatre (named for the late great Al Jolson, then in his heyday
as a Shubert star), it was a surprise click. It premitred on the
heels of another mitzel-Enropa operetta, Madame Pompadour,
by the late Leo Fall, a famed Viennese composer. Pompadour
was in the intra-show biz Broadway spotlight that fall of 1924
because it eclipsed even the sundry Follies of Florenz Ziegfeld
Jr. in opulence, and it was the inaugural attraction of the just-
‘opened Martin Beck Theater. That legit house, still one of the
slickest extant, made show biz history by being built on New
York’s West 45th Street across 8th Avenue, and was optimistic-
ally regarded by Times Square realtors and showmen alike as
paving the way for improving 8th Avenue, something that is
still in the wishful-thinking stage.

Romberg, even then, was burdened by the somewhat libelous
intra-trade tag of a Shubert “hack,” meaning that whenever the
prolific producers needed a musicomedy or operetta score in a
hurry, Romberg was their boy. To his credit, whatever the
pressures, the durability of his music attests to his quality. If
not a Broadway immortal, Romberg is certainly one not to be
forgotten. I has since become axiomatic that “the sun never
sets on a Student Prince company.” ‘The Broadway wisecrack
also applied to “the sun never sets on a Blossom Time company”
and, in later years, a Holly wood-originated legit revue contain-
ed a funny sketch about trying to find a “lost” company of
Blossom Time tcoupers. It is notable that while Romberg
“adapted” che Franz Schubert melodies for Blossom Time,
whose libretto revolved around the Jife and music of the
composer, Student Prince was an original effort.

Variety “raved” when Student Prince sort of sneaked onto
Broadway, albeit eclipsed by the gaudiness and glamour of the

Lanza

aforementioned Leo Fall musical. The Variety critic called it
“spectacular and triumphant in every sense... a musical smash,
colorful, gorgeous and beautiful... For a costumed operetta,
The Student Prince has it all over Madame Pompadour in
entertainment... The Romberg music is popularly pleasing.
Its simplicity and appealing lilt will do much to attract b.9.
(boxoffice) attention. Golden Days, Deep in My Heart, the
Serenade and Just We Two are several of the outstanding
numbers... Although the opening ran from 8:20 to 11:25 it
could be whipped into the necessary time limits if the encores
were omitted. However, the demand seemed to warrant the
chorus repeats, particularly the large ensemble numbers such
as the drinking song and others ... Compared to the § 5.50 scale
for Pompadour, the Heidelberg operetta is a bargain at $ 4.40.”
For the historians, Howard Marsh created the role now sung so
admirably in this album by Mario Lanza. Ilse Marvenga was
the soprano lead, as the innkeeper’s daughter (here sung by
Norma Giusti) whom Prince Karl Franz has to forsake for a
marriage of state to Princess Margaret (Roberta Beatty in the
original). Of such simple triangles were Graustarkian plots spun
in the 1920s, called not for nought the Era of Wonderful
Nonsense.

The original Broadway production achieved the respectable run
of 608 performances in an era when Broadway held eighty to
ninety legitimate theaters instead of the meager thirty or so
today—the others razed or gone the way of TV studios or
movier houses. Incidentally, Student Prince topped the Blossom
Time run of 592 performances,

Old songs like old wine savor well, and when served in the
manner of Mario Lanza & Co,, with Stereophonic high fidelity
recording techniques, this album takes its place with the best of

sound-and-music reprodeutions, ABEL GREEN

Lucio Battisti was born in March
1943 in Poggio Bustone, a little
town in the middle of Italy. In
1950 the family moved to Rome.
Lucio graduated from school
with honours and in accordance
with his father's wishes he be-
came an engineer. In the course
of his studies he began to learn
the guitar and soon music took
over, In spring '65, after his

final courses, he set off for
Milan, Italy's centre of records
and publishing, Ricordi, one of
the most important companies,
brought him in contact with
Mogol, one of the best Italian
\yriciats and soon a fruitful

partnership developed,

Lucio’s first success was as a
composer. 1966 he had three
hits in a row. In 1968 he took
Part in the “Cantagiro”-Festival
and made his breakthrough also
as a singer. Since then each of
his songs has become a hit and
has made number one in the
charts. Also other famous Italian
artists like Mina, Patty Pravo,
and Formula 3 sing his songs
and even England knows him
through his “I! paradiso”. Anien
Corner made a big hit of it as
“If Paradise Were Half As
Nice”. “Billboard”, America’s
music trade magazine,

Lucio with the 1971 “Trend-
setter Award".
Towards the end of 1972 his
album and single “Il mio canto ~
libero” were released. Both re-
cordings stayed several months
on top of the bestseller lists
and the album alone sold

750 000 copies.

His biggest hit ir

as well as his latest release is
“Ancora tu” from his album

“Il contrabasso ...". At the
moment he is in Los Angeles to
record an album in English with
top-producer Bones Howe, to
be released shortly. For Lucio
this is already his second album
in a foreign language. He was
in Hamburg in September 1973
to record a German album
called “Our Free Song” with
lyrics by Udo Lindenberg.
Lucio lives quietly near Milan.
There he owns a house with a
huge garden and a recording
fe Et See
‘out new songs with Mogol.

are painting and photography.
